# VibePicks (full directory)
> Every VibePicks ranking, tool, plain-English reason, pricing label and verified release in one file. Short index: https://vibepicks.ai/llms.txt

Site: https://vibepicks.ai/
Last updated: 2026-10-26
About: VibePicks ranks AI tools for vibe coders, builders and non-coders by use case. #1 is our top pick in each category.
Pricing labels: Free = no paid tier needed; Freemium = usable free plan plus paid upgrades; Paid = paid plan or trial that converts to paid.
Rankings are editorial picks and are never sold. Sponsored placements are always labeled Sponsored.

## Coding Agents & AI IDEs
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/coding-agents/

### #1 Claude Code
- Website: https://claude.com/product/claude-code
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Terminal-based agent for multi-file changes in real repos
- In plain English: Give it a task in plain English and it reads your whole project and makes the changes itself.

### #2 Cursor
- Website: https://cursor.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: AI-first code editor for building and refactoring whole apps
- In plain English: A code editor with AI built in. You type what you want changed and it edits your project for you.

### #3 OpenAI Codex
- Website: https://chatgpt.com/codex
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Delegating coding tasks to a cloud or CLI agent
- In plain English: ChatGPT's coding agent. Hand it a job and it works through it in the background.

### #4 GitHub Copilot
- Website: https://github.com/features/copilot
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Inline completions and agent mode inside VS Code and GitHub
- In plain English: Suggests the next lines of code as you type, so it's a gentle way to start using AI for coding.

### #5 OpenCode
- Website: https://opencode.ai
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Open-source coding agent that works with any AI model
- In plain English: Free, open-source coding helper for your terminal, desktop or editor. Bring any AI model you already pay for (or use its free ones), so you're never locked into one company.

### #6 Google Antigravity
- Website: https://antigravity.google
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Google's agent-first coding app and CLI
- In plain English: Google's coding app where AI agents plan, write and test code for you. The free plan has weekly limits; a Google AI plan gives more.

### #7 Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
- Website: https://devin.ai/desktop
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Agentic IDE for running and managing local and cloud coding agents
- In plain English: An AI code editor that can take on bigger multi-step jobs across your project with little hand-holding.

### #8 Grok Build
- Website: https://x.ai/build
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Terminal-based coding agent from xAI
- In plain English: Works like Claude Code: give it a task in plain English and it plans, edits your project and runs commands. Newer than the others here. A little use is free, and the $8/month Plus plan gives more.

## App Builders
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/app-builders/

### #1 Lovable
- Website: https://lovable.dev
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Prompt-to-full-stack web app with Supabase integration
- In plain English: Easiest place to start: describe your app and it builds a working version you can click around in minutes.

### #2 Bolt.new
- Website: https://bolt.new
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: In-browser prompt-to-app builds you can run and deploy
- In plain English: Type an idea and get a working website or app right in your browser, nothing to install.

### #3 v0
- Website: https://v0.app
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Generating React/Next.js UI and apps from prompts
- In plain English: Great for good-looking websites and pages. Describe the look and it builds it for you.

### #4 Replit
- Website: https://replit.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Cloud IDE with an agent that builds and hosts apps
- In plain English: Build, run and publish an app all in one place in your browser, with an AI helper that does the coding.

## Deploy & Hosting
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/hosting/

### #1 Vercel
- Website: https://vercel.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Deploying Next.js and frontend apps from Git
- In plain English: One click to put your website online with a real link, and it's free for small sites.

### #2 Netlify
- Website: https://www.netlify.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Static sites and Jamstack apps with simple deploys
- In plain English: Drag and drop your site to get it live on the internet. Simple and free to start.

### #3 Cloudflare Workers & Pages
- Website: https://www.cloudflare.com/products/workers/
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Free global hosting for static sites, plus Workers for server code
- In plain English: Free, fast hosting from one of the biggest internet companies. Static files are free and unlimited, and the free plan covers 100,000 server requests a day. Cloudflare now points new projects to Workers.

### #4 Railway
- Website: https://railway.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Deploying backends, workers, and databases with little config
- In plain English: Puts apps that need a server or database online without you managing any computers.

### #5 Render
- Website: https://render.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Hosting web services, cron jobs, and Postgres
- In plain English: A simple place to run your app and its database online, with a free tier to try it.

## Auth
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/auth/

### #1 Clerk
- Website: https://clerk.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Drop-in sign-in UI and user management for React/Next.js
- In plain English: Adds polished sign-up and log-in screens to your app in minutes.

### #2 Supabase Auth
- Website: https://supabase.com/auth
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Auth bundled with your Supabase Postgres database
- In plain English: Free log-ins that come bundled with Supabase, so your accounts and data live in one place.

### #3 Better Auth
- Website: https://better-auth.com
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Free, open-source auth that keeps users in your own database
- In plain English: A free log-in system you add to your own code, so your users and passwords live in your own database. It took over from NextAuth (Auth.js). An optional $20/month dashboard adds logs and security alerts.

### #4 Auth0
- Website: https://auth0.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Enterprise-grade auth, SSO, and identity
- In plain English: Battle-tested log-in system that big companies trust when security really matters.

### #5 Firebase Authentication
- Website: https://firebase.google.com/products/auth
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Simple auth for mobile and web apps on Google's stack
- In plain English: Google's free log-in system, with easy 'Sign in with Google' and phone login.

## Payments & Email
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/payments-email/

### #1 Stripe
- Website: https://stripe.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Accept card payments, subscriptions and checkout links
- In plain English: The standard way to take payments online. Make a payment link with no code, or add checkout to your app. No monthly fee: 2.9% + 30¢ per US card sale.

### #2 Resend
- Website: https://resend.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Send emails from your app: receipts, sign-ups, password resets
- In plain English: The easiest way for an app to send emails, and AI coding tools know it well. Free for 3,000 emails a month (100 a day); $20/month for 50,000.

### #3 Paddle
- Website: https://www.paddle.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Sell software and subscriptions with sales tax handled for you
- In plain English: Paddle becomes the official seller, so it collects and files sales tax and VAT worldwide for you. No monthly fee: 5% + 50¢ per sale.

### #4 Polar
- Website: https://polar.sh
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Sell digital products, licenses and subscriptions, tax handled
- In plain English: Like Paddle but made for developers and indie makers, with clear posted prices. Free to start at 5% + 50¢ per sale, with lower rates on paid plans as you grow.

### #5 Postmark
- Website: https://postmarkapp.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Reliable transactional email for important messages
- In plain English: Known for getting important emails like password resets into the inbox fast. The free plan is 100 emails a month for testing; paid plans start at $15/month for 10,000.

## Databases & Backend
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/databases/

### #1 Supabase
- Website: https://supabase.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Postgres, auth, storage, and realtime in one backend
- In plain English: Stores your app's data plus log-ins and file uploads, all in one free-to-start package.

### #2 Firebase
- Website: https://firebase.google.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Realtime NoSQL backend for quick mobile/web apps
- In plain English: Google's all-in-one backend for saving data, great for phone apps and realtime updates.

### #3 Neon
- Website: https://neon.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Serverless Postgres with branching
- In plain English: A simple online database that's free to start and only charges when it's actually being used.

### #4 Convex
- Website: https://www.convex.dev
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Reactive TypeScript backend with built-in database
- In plain English: A backend where your app's data updates live on screen, without setting up servers.

### #5 PlanetScale
- Website: https://planetscale.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Scalable managed MySQL/Postgres
- In plain English: A heavy-duty database for when your app gets lots of users and needs to stay fast.

## Design-to-Code
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/design-to-code/

### #1 Figma Make
- Website: https://www.figma.com/make/
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Turning prompts and Figma designs into working prototypes
- In plain English: Sketch or describe a screen and it turns it into a working prototype you can click.

### #2 Builder.io
- Website: https://www.builder.io
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Converting Figma designs into framework code
- In plain English: Turns designs into real web pages and lets you edit the site visually, like a page builder.

### #3 Locofy
- Website: https://www.locofy.ai
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Figma/Penpot to React, Next.js, and mobile code
- In plain English: Converts your Figma designs into real app or website code.

### #4 Anima
- Website: https://www.animaapp.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Exporting Figma designs to React/HTML code
- In plain English: Takes a design from Figma and turns it into a working website.

## Testing & QA
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/testing/

### #1 Playwright
- Website: https://playwright.dev
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Reliable end-to-end browser tests (open source)
- In plain English: Free tool that clicks through your site like a real person to catch anything that breaks.

### #2 Cypress
- Website: https://www.cypress.io
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Developer-friendly E2E and component testing
- In plain English: Lets you watch automated tests click through your app so you can see exactly where bugs happen.

### #3 Sentry
- Website: https://sentry.io
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Catching errors and crashes in production
- In plain English: Emails you when your live app crashes and shows exactly what went wrong.

## AI Code Review
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/code-review/

### #1 CodeRabbit
- Website: https://www.coderabbit.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: AI code review on pull requests
- In plain English: An AI reviewer that reads your code changes and points out bugs before they go live. Free for public projects; paid plans start at $24 per developer a month (billed yearly).

### #2 Greptile
- Website: https://www.greptile.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: AI code review that understands your whole codebase
- In plain English: Reviews each change with your whole project in mind, so it catches bugs that only show up across files, with less noise. Free for one developer (50 reviews' worth of credits a month); Pro has no seat fees: you prepay credits at $1 each (a basic review uses 1 credit), shared across your team.

### #3 Cursor Bugbot
- Website: https://cursor.com/bugbot
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Automatic AI review on GitHub pull requests
- In plain English: Cursor's reviewer checks every GitHub pull request for real logic bugs and lets you fix them in one click. Billed from your Cursor plan's usage, about $1 to $1.50 per review.

## LLM APIs
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/llm-apis/

### #1 OpenAI API
- Website: https://platform.openai.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: General-purpose GPT models for chat, tools, and vision
- In plain English: The ChatGPT brain you can plug into your own app or chatbot.

### #2 Anthropic API
- Website: https://claude.com/platform/api
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Claude models, strong at coding and long context
- In plain English: Claude's brain for your own app. Great at writing, reasoning and long documents.

### #3 Google Gemini API
- Website: https://ai.google.dev
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Gemini models with large context and multimodal input
- In plain English: Google's AI with a generous free tier, good for chatbots and reading images or PDFs.

### #4 xAI API
- Website: https://x.ai/api
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Grok models plus image, video and voice on one API key
- In plain English: Grok's AI for your own app. The same key also makes images, video and voice, and it can search the web and X live. Pay as you go, with a free playground to test before you buy.

### #5 DeepSeek API
- Website: https://api-docs.deepseek.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Low-cost models with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs
- In plain English: Very cheap AI for your own app, and it works with code written for OpenAI or Claude. Pay as you go with no free tier, and prices drop by half outside peak hours.

### #6 OpenRouter
- Website: https://openrouter.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: One API key to route across many model providers
- In plain English: One account to try many different AI models and pick the best price for your chatbot.

## AI Images & Art
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/ai-images/

### #1 ChatGPT Images
- Website: https://chatgpt.com/images
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Quick images and edits by chatting
- In plain English: Just describe the picture in plain English and ask for changes like "make it smaller and add a blue outline". Easiest place to start.

### #2 Nano Banana (Gemini)
- Website: https://gemini.google/overview/image-generation/
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Make and edit images by chatting in the Gemini app
- In plain English: Google's image maker inside Gemini. Great at editing your own photos, keeping a character looking the same, and putting clear words in pictures. Free to use; a Google AI plan unlocks the best model and higher limits.

### #3 Midjourney
- Website: https://www.midjourney.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: High-quality illustrations and artistic images
- In plain English: Produces some of the most beautiful, artistic images around. No free plan, so try a free option first.

### #4 FLUX (Black Forest Labs)
- Website: https://bfl.ai
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Photo-real images and an image API with open models
- In plain English: Makes very realistic photos and product shots, and it's one of the cheapest to use in your own app (pay per image, no subscription). Some versions are free to download and run on a powerful computer.

### #5 Ideogram
- Website: https://ideogram.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Logos, stickers, posters and images with readable text
- In plain English: The best at putting real, readable words inside a picture, so it's great for logos, thumbnails and channel art. Free credits every week.

### #6 Grok Imagine
- Website: https://grok.com/imagine
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Quick images from a sentence, right inside Grok
- In plain English: Type what you want and it makes pictures in seconds, then you can ask for changes. The free plan includes a limited number of images a day (xAI doesn't say how many).

### #7 Recraft
- Website: https://www.recraft.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Logos, icons, vector art and brand sets
- In plain English: Makes clean logos and icons that stay sharp at any size, so they look good as tiny emotes and on big banners alike.

### #8 Leonardo
- Website: https://leonardo.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Emotes, game assets, characters and stylized art
- In plain English: Lots of ready-made art styles for cartoons, game items and characters, which makes it easy to get a consistent look for a set of emotes. Free tokens every day.

## AI Audio & Voice
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/ai-audio/

### #1 Suno
- Website: https://suno.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Songs, jingles and background music from a text description
- In plain English: Describe the song you want, like "upbeat 10-second podcast intro jingle", and it makes it with music and even vocals. Free to try; downloading and commercial use need the $10/mo plan.

### #2 ElevenLabs
- Website: https://elevenlabs.io
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Realistic AI voiceovers, narration, sound effects and music
- In plain English: Paste your script and it reads it out in a natural human-sounding voice. Also makes sound effects. Free monthly credits, paid from $6/mo.

### #3 Descript
- Website: https://www.descript.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Edit podcasts and videos by editing the transcript
- In plain English: Turns your recording into text, and you edit the audio just like a document: delete a word and it's gone from the recording. Free plan includes 60 minutes a month.

## AI for Hardware & Electronics
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/ai-hardware/

### #1 Arduino Cloud
- Website: https://cloud.arduino.cc
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Write, upload and control Arduino/ESP32 projects with a built-in AI assistant
- In plain English: Arduino's own online editor has an AI helper that writes and fixes the code for your board, and lets you control wireless (Wi-Fi) projects from your phone. Free plan includes 30 AI requests a month.

### #2 Wokwi
- Website: https://wokwi.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Simulate Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi Pico projects in your browser
- In plain English: Build and test your circuit on screen with virtual boards, sensors and LEDs, including Wi-Fi on the ESP32, so you can't fry real parts while learning. Free for public projects.

### #3 Tinkercad
- Website: https://www.tinkercad.com
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Beginner circuits and 3D-printable designs
- In plain English: Autodesk's free, super-friendly tool for designing parts to 3D print and wiring up practice circuits with a virtual Arduino.

### #4 ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Explain wiring, write firmware and troubleshoot step by step
- In plain English: Describe your parts and what you want them to do and it explains the wiring and writes the board code. You can even send it a photo of your setup when something isn't working.

### #5 Flux
- Website: https://www.flux.ai
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: AI-assisted circuit and PCB design
- In plain English: An AI helper for designing your own custom circuit board, from parts list to a board you can order. Paid after a 14-day free trial (free for students).

### #6 OpenPLC
- Website: https://autonomylogic.com
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Free, open-source PLC you can program with ladder logic
- In plain English: Learn and test PLC programs (ladder logic, structured text) for free without buying an industrial controller. It can run on a regular PC or a Raspberry Pi.

## AI Video & Clips
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/ai-video/

### #1 CapCut
- Website: https://www.capcut.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Edit shorts and reels with auto captions
- In plain English: A free, easy video editor made for TikTok-style videos. Auto captions, templates and simple cuts are on the free plan; some effects need Pro.

### #2 Opus Clip
- Website: https://www.opus.pro
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Turn a long video or stream into short clips
- In plain English: Upload a long video or paste a YouTube link and AI picks the best moments, crops them vertical and adds captions. Free plan gives 60 minutes of video a month, with a watermark.

### #3 Gemini Omni (formerly Veo)
- Website: https://gemini.google/overview/video-generation/
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Realistic AI video clips with sound, made and edited by chatting
- In plain English: Google's video maker in the Gemini app, which replaced Veo. Describe a scene or upload photos and it makes a realistic clip with sound, then you can ask for changes. Needs a paid Google AI plan.

### #4 Kling AI
- Website: https://kling.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Make AI video clips from text or a picture
- In plain English: Makes smooth, realistic clips with good lip-sync at a low price. The free plan lets you try it (watermarked, personal use only), and paid plans start under $10 a month.

### #5 Descript
- Website: https://www.descript.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Edit video by editing the transcript
- In plain English: Your video becomes a text document. Delete words in the text and they're cut from the video. Good for talking videos and podcasts.

### #6 Runway
- Website: https://runway.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Generate short AI video clips from text or images
- In plain English: Makes brand-new video clips from a description or a picture. Free plan is a one-time 125 credits, enough to try a few clips.

### #7 Grok Imagine
- Website: https://grok.com/imagine
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Short AI video clips with sound from text or a picture
- In plain English: Turns a description or a picture into a short clip with sound effects and even talking characters. Video needs the $30/month Premium plan, so try Runway's free credits first.

## Automations & Agents
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/automations/

### #1 Zapier
- Website: https://zapier.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Connect apps with simple if-this-then-that steps
- In plain English: The easiest place to start: pick a trigger and an action and it just runs. Free plan covers 100 tasks a month with two-step automations.

### #2 Make
- Website: https://www.make.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Visual drag-and-drop automations
- In plain English: Draw your automation as a flowchart. More free room than Zapier (1,000 credits a month), a little more to learn.

### #3 n8n
- Website: https://n8n.io
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Powerful automations and AI agents you can host yourself
- In plain English: Very flexible and free if you run it on your own computer or server. The hosted version is a 14-day trial, then paid. Best once you're comfortable.

### #4 Grok Bot
- Website: https://x.ai/bot
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: AI teammates that work in your apps and run routines on a schedule
- In plain English: Instead of building a flowchart, you tell it the job in plain English and it signs into your tools and does it, even on a schedule. VibePicks is built and run with it. It starts at $30/month, and simple fixed tasks are cheaper and more predictable in Zapier or Make.

## Websites & Stores
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/websites/

### #1 Wix
- Website: https://www.wix.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: AI-built business websites with drag-and-drop editing
- In plain English: Describe your business and its AI builds a starter site you can then drag and edit. Free plan works but shows Wix ads and a wixsite.com address.

### #2 Shopify
- Website: https://www.shopify.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Online store to sell products
- In plain English: The standard for selling things online: products, checkout, shipping and payments in one place. Short free trial, then usually $1 a month for 3 months before regular pricing.

### #3 Framer
- Website: https://www.framer.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Good-looking sites and landing pages with AI layouts
- In plain English: Great for a sharp-looking landing page or portfolio. AI can draft the layout for you. Free plan uses a Framer address and badge.

### #4 Squarespace
- Website: https://www.squarespace.com
- Pricing: Paid
- Use it for: Polished templates for a simple business site or shop
- In plain English: Clean, professional templates that are hard to make look bad. No free plan, but there's a 14-day free trial.

## Writing & Marketing
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/writing/

### #1 ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Draft posts, emails and product descriptions
- In plain English: Tell it what you're selling and who it's for and it writes a first draft in seconds. Ask for a few versions and pick the one that sounds most like you.

### #2 Claude
- Website: https://claude.ai
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Natural-sounding writing and rewrites
- In plain English: Good at writing that doesn't sound like a robot, and at rewriting your own draft to be clearer. Free plan has daily limits.

### #3 Gemini
- Website: https://gemini.google.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Drafts and rewrites, built into Gmail and Google Docs
- In plain English: Google's AI assistant. Good for first drafts and rewrites, and handy if you live in Gmail and Google Docs, since paid plans put it right inside them. The free plan has everyday limits.

### #4 Grok
- Website: https://grok.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Timely social posts and replies
- In plain English: A chat assistant like ChatGPT that can read live posts on X and the web, so it's handy for writing about what people are talking about today. The free plan has limited daily use; the $8/month Plus plan gives more.

### #5 Grammarly
- Website: https://www.grammarly.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Fix spelling, grammar and tone as you type
- In plain English: Checks your writing everywhere you type, in email, social posts and docs. The free plan catches spelling and grammar mistakes.

## CAD & Machining
Page: https://vibepicks.ai/cad-machining/

### #1 Fusion
- Website: https://www.autodesk.com/products/fusion-360/personal
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: CAD and CAM in one, from design to toolpaths
- In plain English: Design the part and make the toolpaths in the same program. Free for personal, non-commercial use (under $1,000 a year), with limits like 10 active designs and 3-axis CAM. Its AI Assistant is still a preview, and generative design needs a paid plan.

### #2 Onshape
- Website: https://www.onshape.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Browser-based CAD that runs on any computer
- In plain English: Full 3D CAD in your web browser, no install. Free plan, but your designs are public. Includes an AI Advisor that answers how-to questions.

### #3 Zoo Zookeeper
- Website: https://zoo.dev/zookeeper
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Describe a part in words and get an editable 3D CAD model
- In plain English: Type something like "a flange with 4 bolt holes" and it makes an editable CAD model you can export as STEP. Works best on simple parts. Free plan includes $10 of AI use a month.

### #4 Tinkercad
- Website: https://www.tinkercad.com
- Pricing: Free
- Use it for: Very simple 3D designs for printing
- In plain English: Autodesk's free beginner tool. Not AI, but the easiest way to make a 3D-printable part in an afternoon.

### #5 ChatGPT
- Website: https://chatgpt.com
- Pricing: Freemium
- Use it for: Explain and draft G-code, feeds and speeds
- In plain English: Good for learning what G-code lines do or drafting a simple program from your dimensions and tool. It can get things wrong, so always simulate and dry-run above the part before cutting.
